title: OSHA general industry machine guarding practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry machine guarding practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart O. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: For some reason a machine guard cannot be attached to the machine itself. What does 1910.212(a)(2) require?

options.A: The machine may run without that guard
options.B: The guard must be secured elsewhere
options.C: The operator must hold the guard in place by hand
options.D: A warning sign may be posted in place of the guard

questions.explanation: "Guards shall be affixed to the machine where possible and secured elsewhere if for any reason attachment to the machine is not possible."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.212, General requirements for all machines (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must a revolving drum, barrel or container be guarded under 1910.212(a)(4)?

options.A: With a painted floor line around it
options.B: With a sign telling employees to keep clear
options.C: With a railing at least 7 feet away
options.D: With an enclosure interlocked with the drive mechanism, so it cannot revolve unless the guard enclosure is in place

questions.explanation: "Revolving drums, barrels, and containers shall be guarded by an enclosure which is interlocked with the drive mechanism, so that the barrel, drum, or container cannot revolve unless the guard enclosure is in place."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.212, General requirements for all machines (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the general requirements for machine guards in 1910.212(a)(2), what must a guard itself not do?

options.A: Offer an accident hazard in itself
options.B: Be attached to the machine
options.C: Be made of metal
options.D: Stay in place while the machine runs

questions.explanation: The paragraph states: "The guard shall be such that it does not offer an accident hazard in itself."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.212, General requirements for all machines (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.212(b) require for machines designed for a fixed location?

options.A: They must be painted a safety color
options.B: They must be set on rubber vibration pads
options.C: They must be securely anchored to prevent walking or moving
options.D: They must be registered with the OSHA area office

questions.explanation: "Machines designed for a fixed location shall be securely anchored to prevent walking or moving."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.212, General requirements for all machines (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.213(b)(1), the power control on each woodworking machine must let the operator do what?

options.A: Cut off the power from the machine without leaving his position at the point of operation
options.B: Restart the machine automatically after a power failure
options.C: Change the blade while the machine is running
options.D: Shut down every machine in the shop from one switch

questions.explanation: A mechanical or electrical power control must be provided on each machine "to make it possible for the operator to cut off the power from each machine without leaving his position at the point of operation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.213, Woodworking machinery requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.213 say about an automatic cutoff saw that strokes continuously without the operator being able to control each stroke?

options.A: It may be used if it has a hood
options.B: It may be used for ripping only
options.C: It shall not be used
options.D: It may be used if inspected weekly

questions.explanation: The rule says: "Any automatic cutoff saw that strokes continuously without the operator being able to control each stroke shall not be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.213, Woodworking machinery requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the spreader on a hand-fed circular ripsaw for, according to 1910.213(c)(2)?

options.A: To hold the hood up while the saw runs
options.B: To prevent material from squeezing the saw or being thrown back on the operator
options.C: To measure the width of each cut
options.D: To collect sawdust below the table

questions.explanation: "Each hand-fed circular ripsaw shall be furnished with a spreader to prevent material from squeezing the saw or being thrown back on the operator."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.213, Woodworking machinery requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Gum has adhered to the sides of a woodworking saw. What does 1910.213(s)(1) require?

options.A: The saw may run until the end of the shift
options.B: The saw must be run at reduced speed
options.C: The saw must be sprayed with oil while running
options.D: The saw shall be immediately cleaned

questions.explanation: 1910.213(s)(1) states: "Saws to which gum has adhered on the sides shall be immediately cleaned."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.213, Woodworking machinery requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must happen to a cracked saw in woodworking under 1910.213(s)?

options.A: It may be used for rough cuts only
options.B: It may be run at reduced speed
options.C: It may be used after a wedge is fitted at the collar
options.D: It must be removed from service

questions.explanation: "All cracked saws shall be removed from service." Paragraph (s) also forbids wedges between the saw disk and the collar (a "wobble saw").

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.213, Woodworking machinery requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does 1910.215(a)(5) exclude from the abrasive wheel machinery section?

options.A: Natural sandstone wheels
options.B: Cup wheels (Types 6 and 11)
options.C: Wheels used on bench and floor stands
options.D: Wheels mounted on portable grinders

questions.explanation: Under "Excluded machinery", "Natural sandstone wheels and metal, wooden, cloth, or paper discs, having a layer of abrasive on the surface are not covered by this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.215, Abrasive wheel machinery (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.215(a)(4), when may the work rest of an offhand grinding machine be adjusted?

options.A: While the wheel runs at full speed
options.B: While the wheel is coasting down after shutoff
options.C: Only when the wheel is not in motion
options.D: At any time, if the operator wears a face shield

questions.explanation: "The work rest shall be securely clamped after each adjustment. The adjustment shall not be made with the wheel in motion."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.215, Abrasive wheel machinery (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before an abrasive wheel is mounted, 1910.215(d)(1) requires the spindle speed of the machine to be checked. What must the check make certain of?

options.A: That it matches the speed of the nearest other grinder
options.B: That it does not exceed the maximum operating speed marked on the wheel
options.C: That it is at least twice the speed marked on the wheel
options.D: That it is 10 percent above the speed marked on the wheel

questions.explanation: "The spindle speed of the machine shall be checked before mounting of the wheel to be certain that it does not exceed the maximum operating speed marked on the wheel."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.215, Abrasive wheel machinery (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During the ring test, a wheel sounds cracked (dead) instead of giving a clear ring. What does 1910.215 say?

options.A: It may be used at half its marked speed
options.B: It shall not be used
options.C: It may be used with an extra blotter
options.D: It may be used on a portable grinder only

questions.explanation: Wheels are tapped gently, and "If they sound cracked (dead), they shall not be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.215, Abrasive wheel machinery (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.217(b)(4)(i) require the pedal mechanism of a mechanical power press to be protected?

options.A: To prevent unintended operation from falling or moving objects or by accidental stepping onto the pedal
options.B: By painting the pedal yellow
options.C: By removing the pedal during die setup only
options.D: By placing the pedal at least 10 feet from the press

questions.explanation: "The pedal mechanism shall be protected to prevent unintended operation from falling or moving objects or by accidental stepping onto the pedal."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.217, Mechanical power presses (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When must the employer provide and enforce the use of safety blocks on a mechanical power press?

options.A: Only during continuous production runs
options.B: Only when the press is being moved to a new location
options.C: Only on presses with part revolution clutches
options.D: Whenever dies are being adjusted or repaired in the press

questions.explanation: "The employer shall provide and enforce the use of safety blocks for use whenever dies are being adjusted or repaired in the press."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.217, Mechanical power presses (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Within how many days of the occurrence must an employer report a point-of-operation injury on a mechanical power press?

options.A: 90 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 6 months

questions.explanation: "The employer shall report, within 30 days of the occurrence, all point-of-operation injuries to operators or other employees" to OSHA or to the State agency running an approved plan.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.217, Mechanical power presses (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A flywheel is located above a working area. What does 1910.219(b)(1)(vi) require of the guards installed?

options.A: That they be painted a warning color
options.B: That they include a clear plastic window for inspection
options.C: That they have sufficient strength to hold the weight of the flywheel in the event of a shaft or wheel mounting failure
options.D: That they be removable while the flywheel turns

questions.explanation: "Wherever flywheels are above working areas, guards shall be installed having sufficient strength to hold the weight of the flywheel in the event of a shaft or wheel mounting failure."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.219, Mechanical power-transmission apparatus (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.219(f)(3), power-driven sprocket wheels and chains must be enclosed unless they are what?

options.A: Painted a warning color
options.B: Running at 250 feet per minute or less
options.C: Marked with a danger sign
options.D: More than 7 feet above the floor or platform

questions.explanation: "All sprocket wheels and chains shall be enclosed unless they are more than seven (7) feet above the floor or platform." The paragraph does not apply to manually operated sprockets.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.219, Mechanical power-transmission apparatus (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where explosives, explosive dusts, flammable vapors or flammable liquids exist, which hazard from shafting does 1910.219(p)(2)(ii) say shall be carefully considered?

options.A: Static sparks
options.B: Excess noise
options.C: Glare from polished surfaces
options.D: Vibration of the floor

questions.explanation: "Where explosives, explosive dusts, flammable vapors or flammable liquids exist, the hazard of static sparks from shafting shall be carefully considered."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.219, Mechanical power-transmission apparatus (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.219(p)(7) require of the regular oilers?

options.A: They must work in pairs
options.B: They must wear tight-fitting clothing
options.C: They must oil machinery only while it is running
options.D: They must hold a state oiler license

questions.explanation: "The regular oilers shall wear tight-fitting clothing. Machinery shall be oiled when not in motion, wherever possible."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.219, Mechanical power-transmission apparatus (as of Nov 3, 2026)
